goal: The autopilot and worker console supervisors auto-respawn a dead daemon child while inside the shared crash-loop budget, and stop respawning with a distinct queryable DEAD-after-budget status once the budget is exhausted.

graders.run: uv run pytest packages/flywheel/tests/test_process_supervision.py -k 'respawn_within_window or budget_exhausted or budget_zero_no_respawn'
graders.name: behavior

relevant: packages/flywheel/src/flywheel/_worker_supervisor.py -- WorkerSupervisor.status()/start() and the WorkerState enum gain auto-respawn + the DEAD-after-budget member
packages/flywheel/src/flywheel/_autopilot_supervisor.py -- AutopilotSupervisor.status()/start() and the AutopilotState enum, mirroring the worker change
packages/flywheel/src/flywheel/_dashboard.py -- the status reader that renders supervisor state; it must handle the new status member
packages/flywheel/tests/test_dashboard.py -- keep green; update any exhaustive status-member rendering in the same change
constraints: Consume the shared policy from supervision-policy-core; do not re-implement window/budget counting here. The two supervisors must enforce the SAME policy.

Adding the DEAD-after-budget member to WorkerState/AutopilotState is a shared invariant: every reader of those enums (dashboard, TUI, tests) must handle the new member in THIS change so no slice inherits a red suite.
Auto-respawn must launch a real new child process (a new pid) -- not relabel the DEAD status string. Respawn happens inside status()/the supervise tick without an operator start() call.
Preserve the existing orphan-free group-shutdown path (start_new_session, killpg) unchanged; respawn must not introduce a new base-branch write path.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not change the worker pool here (separate task pool-slot-retirement) or the headless autopilot entrypoint (separate task).
Do not modify or weaken assertions in any existing tests/ file; the orphan-shutdown and DEAD/DETACHED-distinction assertions must stay intact.
Do not auto-START autopilot from a cold console -- the manual-start default is unchanged; this governs respawn of an ALREADY-running daemon only.
Do not add new persistent-store surfaces.
edge_cases: A respawned child that immediately re-dies must count against the same window so the budget can be reached (criterion #2).
Budget 0 / disabled: the supervisor must reproduce today's plain DEAD behavior exactly (no respawn).
After exhaustion the supervisor must STOP spawning -- a later operator start() may still re-arm it, but no automatic spawn occurs.
